title: Uptown dance halls versus downtown
summary: Asked about uptown dances, he names halls and a Perdido Street dance, saying uptown bands played mostly blues.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, Drag, can you tell me, did you ever get uptown when you were young to go to dances, like up at the Masonic Hall or any place uptown? I've been all uptown.

I've been all to Masonic, Globesaw, and New Hall and all them places, downtown, I've been all over. I wonder if you ever went uptown and heard the dances up there too, danced up there. Yeah, like there's a place called, what used to call, it's been on Frankie Street. On Frankie Street, on Frankie Street, let me see, it was, it's called, a lot of times ago, but it's called, I used to call that name. Yes, well, I know the one you mean. The Funky Butthole. The Funky Butthole. The Funky Butthole, on Perdido. Perdido Street, yeah, between the ramparts and the side too, I used to go all the whole time. It used to have nothing but posters.
Was the dancing any different up there than downtown in Deconomy Hall?

Oh yeah, the way you ever see, but the people on that dance, more, it used to be more butter bone playing, bands playing down there, and what, I mean, Ferry Capon used to play like that, nothing but the blues.
